sections.title: The signal path, measured rather than assumed

sections.intro: The headline is negative and it is the most important result in this report.

refusals.name: every per-pixel noise statistic, on most of the set
refusals.reason: Of 365 clips, 28 support the noise table above. The exclusions overlap, so these counts do not partition the set: **81** are moving, and ME.1b's gate correctly keeps every per-pixel temporal statistic off a clip whose scene is sliding across the pixels; **306** have a robust noise scale at or below *one code*, which means the codec has removed the sensor's noise entirely -- no window can meet a threshold written in units of a ruler that has collapsed onto the quantiser, and the flat-region finder refusing is the correct answer rather than a tuning problem; **30** have a usable ruler but no window flat enough against it. Every value in the table is an upper bound on what the codec left, not a measurement of the camera.

sections.intro: What the FFC leaves in a ten-second clip.

refusals.name: FFC interval distribution
refusals.reason: The clips are ten seconds long and `freeze_intervals_s` refuses anything under 180 s -- the Boson's own schedule -- so this set gives freeze *length* and can never give an interval. That is a property of the publication, not of the analyser.

refusals.name: between-FFC pattern growth
refusals.reason: `fit_pattern_growth` needs the resets to fit sigma^2(t) between them. A ten-second clip at a 180 s schedule contains at most one, so there is no growth curve in it.

statistics.name: freeze length
statistics.note: mean over the events in a clip

statistics.name: pattern change across a freeze
statistics.note: below ~2.5 the freeze is a stall, above ~5 a shutter (ME.3a); 5 clips dropped as non-finite

sections.title: The shutter signature

sections.intro: This is where the reference set stops being usable, and the reason is worth recording.

refusals.name: target size, SCR, contrast polarity, edge spread and smear
refusals.reason: All five need the annotation boxes. The labels ship as MATLAB Video Labeler `groundTruth` objects -- MCOS class instances inside `__function_workspace__` -- which `scipy.io.loadmat` returns as an opaque blob and no Python reader decodes. The index said a Python decoder ships with the dataset; **it does not** (the repository ships a MATLAB script, `Create_a_dataset_from_videos_and_labels.m`), and the index has been corrected. Decoding MCOS is possible and is not worth its own failure mode here: until someone runs the MATLAB script and exports boxes, every box-dependent Tier 4 comparison is open.

refusals.name: sky elevation profile and cloud clutter slope
refusals.reason: Both need a labelled sky region and, for the profile, a visible horizon. Selecting either automatically would be inventing an annotation and calling it data. The analysers are implemented and tested (ME.4); what is missing is a region list.

refusals.name: size and SCR versus range
refusals.reason: Needs LRDDv3's range labels, which sit behind an access request citing export control. Unavailable, not unimplemented.
